title: File-System Operations
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of file-system operations in a Classic ASP application.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will study file-system operations as part of Classic ASP development and legacy maintenance. The lesson follows the attached ASP curriculum topic 79 and uses the syllabus subtopics as the coverage checklist.
content.why_it_matters: File-System Operations matters because Classic ASP behavior crosses a server-side scripting engine, IIS configuration, request/response boundaries, and often COM or ADO dependencies. A small, explicit test helps distinguish intended behavior from runtime-specific behavior.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Classic ASP often relies on Windows COM components and external services for file operations, messaging, XML, and integration. For 'File-System Operations', document the exact component/provider version, permissions, bitness, network boundaries, timeouts, and recovery behavior. Never construct a filesystem path or external URL directly from untrusted input, and keep secrets outside the public web root and repository.

content_blocks.title: Syllabus coverage
content_blocks.text: The lesson explicitly covers: Introduction to Scripting.FileSystemObject; Working with directories; Reading text files; Writing text files; Checking file existence; File and folder permissions; Safely resolving file paths. Treat these subtopics as connected requirements. For each one, be able to define the concept, identify where it appears in a Classic ASP application, and name one test or diagnostic that would verify it.

content_blocks.title: Inspectable example: File-System Operations
content_blocks.code:
<%
Dim fso, fileObj, fixedPath
fixedPath = "D:\CodeLeafData\sample.txt"
Set fso = Server.CreateObject("Scripting.FileSystemObject")
If fso.FileExists(fixedPath) Then
  Set fileObj = fso.OpenTextFile(fixedPath, 1, False)
  Response.Write Server.HTMLEncode(fileObj.ReadAll)
  fileObj.Close
  Set fileObj = Nothing
End If
Set fso = Nothing
%>

content_blocks.run_instructions: The path is illustrative and must point outside the public web root with restrictive ACLs. Never accept a raw client file path. The standard CodeLeaf browser playground previews HTML/CSS/JavaScript only; it does not execute Classic ASP, VBScript, ADO, IIS commands, PowerShell, or SQL. content_blocks.text: Use approved test data and a component/service you control. Confirm path permissions, host allow-lists, timeouts, malformed responses, and cleanup behavior. common_mistakes.problem: Treating legacy runtime behavior as universal.
common_mistakes.why: IIS versions, Windows lifecycle, COM registration/bitness, and ADO providers can change behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Write down the actual server/provider versions and validate on a disposable test site.

common_mistakes.why: Empty input, missing records, expired sessions, permissions, timeouts, and malformed data reveal different failure modes.
common_mistakes.fix: Add normal, negative, and boundary cases with expected outcomes.

common_mistakes.why: Detailed errors can reveal paths, SQL text, configuration, and component information.
common_mistakes.fix: Keep diagnostics in restricted server-side logs and return a generic message with a reference ID.
